name: Abishai
bio:
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, a warrior under David who later became one of the fiercest commanders in David's army. When Saul pursued David with three thousand chosen men into the wilderness of Ziph, David asked who would go down with him into Saul's camp, and Abishai volunteered at once: "I'll go with you" (1 Samuel 26:6). The two slipped in by night and found Saul and his army fast asleep; Abishai told David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hands this day. Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear; I won't strike him twice." David stopped him, refusing to harm "the LORD's anointed," and instead took only Saul's spear and water jug before leaving (1 Samuel 26:7-12). This scene reveals Abishai's bold, combative nature, in contrast to David's greater restraint. After Saul's death, Abishai joined his brothers Joab and Asahel in pursuing Abner, who had installed Ish-Bosheth as king; after Abner killed Asahel, Joab and Abishai continued the chase until Abner pleaded for peace and Joab sounded the retreat (2 Samuel 2:18-28). When Joab later lured Abner aside and killed him in revenge for Asahel, David sharply condemned the assassination, yet could only say, "These sons of Zeruiah are too strong for me" (2 Samuel 3:22-39) — a verdict Abishai, as one of Zeruiah's three sons, shared alongside his brother Joab.

When the Ammonites hired Aramean mercenaries to fight alongside them against Israel, Joab divided the army in two: he himself faced the Arameans, while he put Abishai in command of the rest to face the Ammonites, with each brother promising to help the other if either front grew too hard-pressed. Both forces fled before Israel that day (2 Samuel 10:9-14). His continued role in David's army unfolds in detail through the rest of 2 Samuel.
